title: The Postcard of Port Alder
premise: Jude Quintana, a cellist whose hands failed them during a career-defining concert, retreats to the fog-bound town of Port Alder to settle their late grandmother's house. There they find an unsent postcard from eleven years ago, addressed to a stranger named Wren Halloway, hinting at a secret inheritance and a love their grandmother abandoned. As Jude searches for Wren, they fall for ferry mechanic Sable Ives, who knew both women and guards a truth about why the postcard was never sent. When Jude's old orchestra offers a second chance timed to the last ferry of the season, they must choose between reclaiming the stage and staying for the family—and the person—they've only just found. In the end, Jude plays one final private concert on the dock, chooses Port Alder, and learns the inheritance was never money but the grandmother's unfinished letter, which Jude finally delivers by hand.
about_author: Mirabel Lockridge is the pen name of a former lighthouse keeper's assistant who writes romances set in coastal towns where weather does half the emotional labor. She lives with two opinionated gulls she refuses to call pets.

chapters.title: The Silence After the Cadence
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Flashback to the catastrophic final performance: mid-concerto, their hands simply stop. The emotional beat is shame crystallizing into a vow that the heart, like any muscle, can be trained into obedience.

chapters.title: A House That Outlived Its Music
chapters.summary: Jude arrives in rain-soaked Port Alder to inventory their grandmother Odile's house. Every room holds sheet music annotated in a stranger's handwriting. Beat: grief tangled with curiosity.

chapters.title: Postmarked Eleven Years Ago
chapters.summary: Behind a loose floorboard, Jude finds an unsent postcard addressed to Wren Halloway, promising 'what I owed you.' POV Jude. Beat: the first crack in their contain-the-heart philosophy.

chapters.title: The Ferry Mechanic
chapters.summary: Sable Ives fixes Jude's rental car and recognizes Odile's name instantly, then goes quiet. POV alternates to Sable, who decides not to say what she knows. Beat: attraction shadowed by withheld history.

chapters.title: Nobody Named Halloway
chapters.summary: Jude canvasses the town; everyone deflects. The postmistress burns red at the name. Beat: frustration hardening into obsession—Jude treats the search like rehearsal, methodical and armored.

chapters.title: Salt and Rosin
chapters.summary: Sable invites Jude to hear the tide organs on the breakwater. Jude plays cello for the first time since the failure, badly, and doesn't die of it. Beat: cautious joy, the heart doing unauthorized things.

chapters.title: What Odile Kept
chapters.summary: In the attic, Jude finds decades of letters between Odile and Wren—love letters, cut off abruptly in year three. POV Jude. Beat: realizing their grandmother had a whole self they never knew.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Left
chapters.summary: Sable finally admits Wren Halloway was her aunt, who left town pregnant and disgraced after Odile chose her music career over her. Beat: betrayal reframes everything; Sable resents Odile, and now Jude by association.

chapters.title: Intermission
chapters.summary: Jude withdraws to the house, playing through Odile's annotated scores and finding instructions hidden in the margins—a map of sorts. Beat: discipline as avoidance; they almost book a flight back to the orchestra.

chapters.title: The Marginalia Sonata
chapters.summary: Decoding the margins reveals Odile composed a piece for Wren and hid its manuscript 'where the ferries sleep.' Jude tells Sable; the ice thaws slightly. Beat: shared purpose replacing suspicion.

chapters.title: Where the Ferries Sleep
chapters.summary: Low tide exposes the derelict boathouse; inside, the manuscript and a second postcard—sent this time, returned unopened. Beat: awe curdling into dread about what Wren never got to read.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: They find Wren Halloway alive, two towns over, running a nursery. She refuses to discuss Odile. POV shifts to Wren briefly: eleven years of practiced indifference cracking at the sight of Odile's handwriting. Beat: hope meeting a locked door.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Jude's conductor calls: principal chair, auditions in ten days—the same day as the last ferry of the season. Beat: the old life making its claim; Jude says yes before their heart can object.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for Leaving
chapters.summary: Jude practices obsessively while avoiding Sable, who sees through it. A near-kiss interrupted by Jude's own retreat. Beat: self-sabotage; the trained heart winning, miserably.

chapters.title: Sable's Version
chapters.summary: Sable confesses she read the unsent postcard years ago and put it back, believing some doors should stay shut to protect Wren. Beat: guilt, anger, and the question—who gets to decide what others can bear?

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: A storm cancels ferries; Jude, Sable, and Wren are stranded together at the house when the power fails. Candlelight, Odile's scores, forced proximity. Beat: truths surfacing faster than anyone can cap them.

chapters.title: What the Letter Said
chapters.summary: Among the manuscripts they find Odile's actual final letter: she didn't choose music over Wren—she was dying of the illness that would later take her, and sent nothing to spare Wren grief. Beat: devastation and release; the villain was time.

chapters.title: The Audition
chapters.summary: Jude travels inland, plays flawlessly, and is offered everything they lost. Walking out with the contract unsigned, they realize the muscle metaphor was wrong: hearts aren't trained, they're trusted. Beat: climax of identity.

chapters.title: Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Race against the schedule; the ferry is casting off as Jude arrives. Sable, working the dock, holds the line an extra thirty seconds. Beat: the choice made physical—Jude steps aboard not to leave but to bring the contract back home.

chapters.title: Delivered by Hand
chapters.summary: Jude reads Odile's letter aloud to Wren at the grave, then gives her the manuscript. Wren weeps, forgives, and asks to hear it played. Beat: inheritance fulfilled—not property but voice, passed down.

chapters.title: Concerto for a Dock
chapters.summary: Jude performs Odile's piece on the breakwater at dawn, the whole town gathered, Sable beside the tide organs. Beat: catharsis; the failed hands play perfectly because there is nothing left to protect.

chapters.title: Winter Residents
chapters.summary: Epilogue, spring. Jude teaches cello at the island school, the house full of students and noise. Final image: a new postcard, written and stamped and actually mailed—to no one in particular, just to prove some words should travel. Beat: belonging, chosen daily.
